message.content:
A prior agent black-box probed the jsonschema behavior family "error-counting-deep" of the program at /workspace/dataset/test13_executable (usage: /workspace/dataset/test13_executable --a '<instance json>' --b '<schema json>'; prints validator class, True/False, top-level error count).

Its findings were:
---
FILE: /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl — 709 vectors, all re-verified reproducible (random 1-in-17 resample: 0 mismatches). 661 exit-0, 48 exit-1 crashes. Invariant holds in every single vector: line2 == "True" IFF line3 == "0". Max observed count 20.

THE CORE RULE. Every keyword validator is a generator. `len(list(iter_errors(instance)))` = the sum over all keywords present in the ROOT schema (in schema dict order, order irrelevant to count) of the number of errors that keyword's generator yields. A keyword is either DESCENDING (it re-runs the whole validator on a child instance/subschema and re-yields every produced error unchanged, so counts multiply/sum recursively without bound) or COLLAPSING (it swallows all sub-errors into a single ValidationError whose .context holds them, contributing at most 1).

DESCENDING KEYWORDS (nested errors bubble up as separate top-level errors):
properties (sum over listed props present in instance), patternProperties (sum over every (pattern, matching prop) pair — a prop matching 2 patterns is validated twice and BOTH sets of errors count; no dedup), additionalProperties WHEN ITS VALUE IS AN OBJECT (sum over each additional prop), items in schema form (sum over every element), items in array/tuple form (drafts 3/4/6/7/2019 only — sum over zip(schemas, elements)), prefixItems (2020-12 only), additionalItems in schema form (drafts 3–2019; sum over each extra element beyond the tuple), propertyNames (sum over every property NAME validated as a string — 3 names x 2 failing keywords = 6), allOf (sum over all branches; it does NOT short-circuit), if/then and if/else (the chosen branch's errors are yielded raw — `then` failing 3 keywords => 3 top-level errors; the `if` subschema's own errors are always discarded and contribute 0), $ref / $dynamicRef (the target schema's errors are yielded raw), dependencies in SCHEMA form (drafts 3/4/6/7 only), dependentSchemas (2019/2020 only), extends (draft 3 only; object or array form, sum over all).

COLLAPSING KEYWORDS (exactly 0 or 1 error, no matter how deep or how many sub-failures):
anyOf (1), oneOf (1, whether 0 branches match or >1 match), not (1), contains (1 — never one-per-element; also 1 when the array is empty, 1 when minContains/maxContains are violated, and if contains + minContains + maxContains all conceptually fail it is still exactly 1 total), unevaluatedProperties (1 total whether false or a schema, whether 1 or 3 unevaluated props each failing 3 keywords), unevaluatedItems (1 total), additionalProperties WHEN false (1 total no matter how many extras: 3 or 5 extras => 1), additionalItems: false (1 total no matter how many extra elements), items: false IN 2020-12 ONLY (1 total — jsonschema special-cases `items is False` into one "Expected at most N items but found M extra" error), type (1, including list form), enum (1, including enum: []), const (1), format (ALWAYS 0 — no FormatChecker is attached), all scalar bounds (minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum/multipleOf/divisibleBy/minLength/maxLength/pattern/minItems/maxItems/uniqueItems/minProperties/maxProperties), disallow (draft 3, 1).

PER-ITEM COLLECTIONS (one error per missing key, not one per keyword):
required as an array yields exactly one error PER missing key (3 missing => 3; 12 missing => 12). dependencies in ARRAY form (d3–d7) yields one error per missing dependent key per trigger key ({a:[x,y],b:[z,w]} with a,b present => 4). dependentRequired (2019/2020) same. draft-3 `required: true` inside properties yields 1 error per missing property.

MEASURED EXAMPLES (2020-12 unless noted): N sibling failing keywords at root => exactly N (verified 1..8: {type,minLength,pattern,enum,maxLength,const} on "ab" => 6; 8 numeric siblings on 7 => 8). properties with N failing children each failing M keywords => N*M (3x3 => 9, 2x2 => 4). items schema with N elements each failing M => N*M (3x3 => 9, 10 items x 2 kw => 20). Nesting is fully multiplicative: 2 items x 2 props x 2 kw => 8; 3 items x 2 props x 2 kw => 12; items(2) x properties x allOf(3) => 6; items(3) x properties x allOf(3) => 9; items(2) x properties x if/then(allOf 3) => 6; items(2) x properties x $ref(2 kw) => 4. Depth is unbounded and does not collapse: 40-level nested properties => 1; 200-level nested allOf => 1; 3-level nested properties with a leaf failing 3 keywords => 3; 4-level => 3; failing 3 sibling keywords at each of 3 object levels plus a 3-failure leaf => 12. Collapsers absorb arbitrary depth: anyOf/oneOf/not/contains/unevaluatedProperties wrapping a subtree that would produce 6 errors each produce exactly 1; the same subtree under allOf/if-then/$ref/dependentSchemas produces 6.

COMBINATION ARITHMETIC (all additive at the same level): properties+patternProperties+additionalProperties:false on {a:1,ab:2,zz:3} => 4 (1 + 2 + 1); adding a second overlapping pattern => 5; patternProperties+additionalProperties(schema) => 3; items(3 fails)+contains(1)+minItems(1) => 5; propertyNames(2)+required(1)+additionalProperties:false(1) => 4; minProperties+maxProperties+required(2 missing)+additionalProperties:false+propertyNames(2)+type => 8; minItems+maxItems+uniqueItems+items(2)+contains+type => 7; 5 propertyNames failures + 5 additionalProperties failures => 10. A "monster" schema (root type + required + property with type + minItems + 2 items x (allOf 2 + if/then 1)) => 10, exactly the sum of parts.

DRAFT DIFFERENCES THAT CHANGE THE COUNT:
- items array/tuple form: works in d3/d4/d6/d7/2019 (descends, N errors); in 2020-12 it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' in referencing/_dollar_id), exit 1.
- items: false => 3 errors for a 3-element array in d6/d7/2019 (boolean schema descended per element), but exactly 1 error in 2020-12. items: false/true CRASHES in d3/d4 (booleans are not valid schemas there; TypeError).
- prefixItems: only recognized in 2020-12 (2 failing prefix items => 2); ignored (0) in d3..2019.
- additionalItems: recognized d3..2019 (false => 1 error total; schema form => 1 per extra element); ignored in 2020-12. Ignored everywhere if `items` is absent or is a schema (not tuple).
- dependencies: active d3/d4/d6/d7 (array form = per missing key; schema form descends); COMPLETELY IGNORED (0 errors) in 2019-09 and 2020-12. String shorthand ("a":"b") works only in d3 (1 error); in d4+ it CRASHES (AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get').
- dependentRequired / dependentSchemas: only 2019/2020 (0 in d3..d7).
- if/then/else: only d7/2019/2020 (0 in d3/d4/d6).
- contains: only d6+; minContains/maxContains only 2019/2020 (ignored in d6/d7). contains on a non-array instance yields 0. minContains:0 makes contains vacuously satisfiable => 0.
- propertyNames: only d6+ (0 in d3/d4).
- unevaluatedProperties / unevaluatedItems: only 2019/2020 (0 in d3..d7).
- required as an array: d4+ (ignored in d3, which uses `required: true` inside each property schema).
- allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not: d4+ (all ignored -> 0 errors in draft 3, which uses `extends`/`disallow` instead).
- const: d6+ (ignored in d3/d4). exclusiveMinimum/Maximum as numbers: d6+; as booleans (modifier on minimum/maximum): d3/d4. divisibleBy: d3 only; multipleOf: d4+ (each ignored in the other).
- extends and disallow: draft 3 only. extends descends (array of 3 failing subschemas => 3); disallow yields 1.
- maxProperties/minProperties: d4+ (0 in d3).
- $ref SIBLING KEYWORDS: in d3/d4/d6/d7 all sibling keywords next to $ref are IGNORED, so {$ref: passing, type:"boolean", minLength:9, pattern:"^q"} => 0 errors; in 2019/2020 siblings are evaluated => 3 errors. With a $ref producing 2 errors plus 2 failing siblings: d3-d7 => 2, 2019/2020 => 4.
- anyOf/oneOf/allOf empty arrays: allOf:[] => valid (0); anyOf:[] => 1 error; oneOf:[] => 1 error (d4+; all 0 in d3 since the keywords don't exist).

SHORT-CIRCUITING (observable via crash propagation): anyOf STOPS at the first passing branch — {anyOf:[{type:"string"},{pattern:"["}]} on "x" returns valid, while reversing the order crashes on the bad regex. oneOf does NOT stop (it must count matches) and crashes. allOf does NOT stop and crashes. not evaluates its subschema and crashes. if/then/else evaluates only the selected branch: with `if` false and no `else`, `then` is never evaluated (a crashing `then` never fires). additionalProperties with a crashing schema never fires if there are no additional properties.

CRASH BEHAVIOR (48 vectors; all exit code 1, full Python traceback on stderr, ZERO stdout because the three prints happen only after both is_valid and iter_errors complete; note is_valid runs first and short-circuits, so a schema can be "invalid-detectable" and still crash during iter_errors): unknown type name {"type":"nosuchtype"} => UndefinedTypeCheck; invalid regex in pattern or a patternProperties key => re.error; enum non-array => TypeError 'int' object is not iterable; allOf/anyOf/oneOf non-array => TypeError not iterable; allOf:[5] (non-schema element) => AttributeError 'int' object has no attribute 'get'; not: 5 => TypeError argument of type 'int' is not iterable; multipleOf: 0 => ZeroDivisionError; top-level schema that is a number/string/array/null => TypeError argument of type 'X' is not iterable (only objects and booleans are valid schemas); properties: 5 or a non-schema subschema value (and analogously items/contains/propertyNames/dependentSchemas/unevaluatedProperties/patternProperties given a scalar) => TypeError/AttributeError — BUT ONLY IF the instance is of the right type to trigger the keyword (e.g. {"properties":5} with instance 1 short-circuits on the non-object instance and prints True/0 with no crash); minLength/minimum/maxItems given a string => TypeError comparison; unresolvable $ref => _WrappedReferencingError PointerToNowhere; a self-referential $ref loop ({$ref:"#/$defs/A",$defs:{A:{$ref:"#/$defs/A"}}}) and $recursiveRef:"#" with $recursiveAnchor => RecursionError; malformed/empty JSON in --a or --b => json.decoder.JSONDecodeError. Non-crashing malformed values: {"additionalProperties":5} is silently ignored (0 errors, because the impl only descends when the value is an object and only errors when it is falsy); {"required":"abc"} on {a:1} iterates the STRING as a sequence of characters and yields 2 errors (for 'b' and 'c'); {"type":[]} yields 1 error; {"properties":5} on a non-object instance yields 0.

OTHER ZERO-COUNT FACTS: unknown keywords, $comment/title/description/default/examples, contentEncoding/contentMediaType, and definitions/$defs blocks that are never $ref'd all contribute 0. format never fails. A recursive $ref that terminates works fine. $id/id do not change counts. Duplicate identical errors are never deduplicated (allOf of two identical failing properties => 2).
---
Gotchas it listed: ["additionalProperties:false yields exactly ONE error listing all unexpected properties, not one per extra property (3 extras => 1). But additionalProperties:{schema} DESCENDS and yields one error set per extra property (3 extras x 3 failing keywords => 9).","items:false is asymmetric across drafts: 1 error total in 2020-12 (special-cased 'Expected at most N items but found M extra'), but 3 errors for a 3-element array in draft-06/07/2019 (boolean schema descended per element), and a hard CRASH in draft-03/04 where booleans are not schemas.","items in array/tuple form CRASHES (exit 1, AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get') under 2020-12 / no-$schema. It is not merely ignored.","if/then/else DESCENDS - `then` failing 3 keywords produces 3 separate top-level errors, not 1. Only anyOf/oneOf/not wrap. The `if` subschema's own errors are always discarded.","contains yields exactly 1 error regardless of array length or how badly each element fails, and also exactly 1 when contains + minContains + maxContains would all fail simultaneously.","unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems yield exactly 1 error even in SCHEMA form (not just false form) and even with 3 unevaluated properties each failing 3 keywords. Easy to wrongly implement as a descend.","patternProperties does not deduplicate: one property matching two patterns is validated against both and both error sets count (1 prop, 2 patterns, 2 failing keywords each => 4).","required with a non-array string value iterates the string's characters: {\"required\":\"abc\"} on {a:1} yields 2 errors, not a crash.","$ref siblings: drafts 3/4/6/7 IGNORE every sibling keyword of $ref (a $ref-passing schema with 3 failing siblings => 0 errors); 2019-09/2020-12 evaluate them (=> 3 errors).","dependencies is fully IGNORED (0 errors) in 2019-09 and 2020-12; dependentRequired/dependentSchemas are ignored in draft 3/4/6/7. dependencies string-shorthand works only in draft 3 and CRASHES in draft 4+.","anyOf short-circuits on the first passing branch (a crashing later branch is never reached), but oneOf, allOf and not evaluate everything and will crash. This is observable only via malformed-subschema probes.","Keyword validators short-circuit on instance type first: {\"properties\":5} or {\"minLength\":\"a\"} only crash when the instance is an object / string respectively; otherwise they silently yield 0.","stdout is EMPTY on any crash - the three print() calls run only after both is_valid() and list(iter_errors()) succeed, so a partially valid result is never printed. Exit code 1, traceback on stderr.","additionalProperties given a non-object, non-false value (e.g. 5) is silently ignored (0 errors) rather than crashing, because the implementation only descends for object values and only errors for falsy values.","format never produces an error in any draft (no FormatChecker is attached), so it always contributes 0 to the count.","allOf:[] is valid (0 errors) but anyOf:[] and oneOf:[] each yield 1 error.","A top-level schema that is a JSON number, string, array or null crashes with TypeError; only objects and the booleans true/false are accepted.","propertyNames descends into each property NAME as a string instance, so 3 names x 2 failing string keywords => 6 errors; it is a multiplier, not a collapser."]
Its vectors are in /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl (709 lines of JSONL, each {"a","b","out","exit"}).

You are the COMPLETENESS CRITIC. Its assignment was:
The precise TOP-LEVEL ERROR COUNT rule — this is the single most important output.
Systematically build schemas of increasing nesting depth and record counts. Cases to cover:
- N sibling keywords failing at the root (type + minLength + pattern + enum) => N?
- properties with N failing children, each child failing M keywords => N*M?
- items array with N failing elements each failing M keywords
- nested properties 3 levels deep with multiple failures at the leaf
- allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not at various depths, including allOf inside properties inside items
- if/then where then fails 3 keywords
- $ref pointing to a schema failing 3 keywords
- patternProperties + additionalProperties both failing
- dependencies schema-form failing multiple keywords
- contains failing (how many errors when no element matches? one, or one per element?)
- propertyNames failing for 3 property names
- unevaluatedProperties with 3 unevaluated props
- 'required' missing 3 keys, additionalProperties:false with 3 extras, uniqueItems + minItems together
Derive and state the general rule (which keyword validators yield descended errors vs a single wrapping error), and enumerate exactly which keywords collapse to 1 error.
Report every case as a vector.

Your job: find what is MISSING or WRONG. Specifically:
1. Read /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl (use head/wc/grep, don't dump the whole thing) and check which parts of the assignment were actually probed.
2. Identify untested edges, especially anything affecting ERROR COUNTS or cross-draft differences, and anything a JavaScript reimplementer would get wrong (unicode string length with astral chars, Python regex vs JS regex, float precision, integer vs bool, object key ordering, deep equality of numbers 1 vs 1.0, -0).
3. RUN those missing probes yourself against the executable and APPEND them as JSONL lines to the SAME file /workspace/probes/error-counting-deep.jsonl (same format: {"a","b","out","exit"}). Use a node script with execFileSync to append so escaping is exact. Never hand-write expected output.
4. Verify a random sample of ~8 existing lines by re-running them and comparing to the recorded "out" — report any mismatch (a mismatch means the file is corrupt/hand-written).

Return: family name, MERGED and CORRECTED findings prose (restate the full spec for this family incorporating both the prior findings and everything new you learned — the implementer reads ONLY your version, so it must be self-contained and complete), the vector file path, the TOTAL line count after your appends (wc -l), and a gotchas list.

import argparse
import json
import jsonschema
from jsonschema import Draft7Validator, validators

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True, help='instance (JSON string)')
parser.add_argument('--b', type=str, required=True, help='schema (JSON string)')
args = parser.parse_args()

instance = json.loads(args.a)
schema = json.loads(args.b)

# Use validator_for to get appropriate validator class
validator_class = validators.validator_for(schema)  # Get validator class for schema
validator = validator_class(schema)  # Create instance

result = validator.is_valid(instance)  # Validate
errors = list(validator.iter_errors(instance))  # Get errors

print(validator_class.__name__)
print(result)
print(len(errors))
